intro: Connectors to tell the result, and «tan… que» for a result that comes from intensity.
p.así que.consejo: It joins a cause with its result in speech: «perdí el autobús, así que llegué tarde».
p.por lo tanto.consejo: It is more formal than «así que». It is used in written texts and speeches.
p.entonces.consejo: It is used to draw a conclusion: «Entonces, nos vamos». It sounds th in Spain: en-TON-thes.
p.o sea que.consejo: It is very common in speech to draw a conclusion: «o sea que no vienes».
p.total que.consejo: It sums up a story in an informal tone: «total, que llegamos tarde».
p.por consiguiente.consejo: Very formal: it appears in reports and letters, almost never in speech.
p.tan.consejo: It goes before an adjective or adverb and never changes: «tan cansado», «tan deprisa».
p.tanto.consejo: With a noun it agrees with it: «tanta gente», «tantos coches». After a verb it does not change.
p.sueño.consejo: «Tener sueño» means to feel sleepy. It is also what you see while you sleep.
p.despertador.consejo: It comes from «despertar». The stress is at the end: des-per-ta-DOR.
p.enfadado.consejo: You say «estar enfadado». In the Americas you also hear «enojado».
p.sonar.consejo: It is irregular: «suena», but «sonó» does not change. The alarm clock «suena».
b1.texto:
These connectors join a cause with its result:

- **In conversation:** así que, por eso, entonces.
- **Very colloquial:** o sea que, total, que.
- **In formal texts:** por lo tanto, por consiguiente.

Perdí el autobús, **así que** llegué tarde.

For a result of intensity use **tan** + adjective + **que** (estaba **tan** cansado **que** me dormí) or **tanto** + noun + **que** (había **tanta** gente **que** no entramos).
b2.f0.texto: I did not hear the alarm clock, so I arrived late.
b2.f1.texto: That is why the boss is angry.
b2.f2.texto: I was so sleepy that I heard nothing.
b2.f3.texto: And there was so much traffic that the bus was late.
b2.f4.texto: Then you finish work later today.
b2.f5.texto: So I cannot have dinner with you today.
b2.f6.texto: You are so tired that the same will happen to you tomorrow.
b2.f7.texto: So, in the end, we are going to buy a new alarm clock.
b4.texto:
- **Tan** goes with an adjective or an adverb and **does not change**: tan cansado, tan despacio.
- **Tanto** goes with a noun and **agrees** with it: tanto ruido, tanta gente, tantos coches, tantas cosas.
- After a verb, **tanto** does not change: comí **tanto** que no pude cenar.

In all three cases the result starts with **que**. When you tell a real result, the verb is indicative.
b4.e0.texto: I was so tired that I fell asleep.
b4.e1.texto: There were so many people that we could not get in.
b4.e2.texto: I missed the bus, so I arrived late.
b5.f0.texto: A grey light comes in through the blind and draws pale stripes on the bed.
b5.f1.texto: The alarm clock keeps an absolute silence on the bedside table.
b5.f2.texto: Pablo sleeps so deeply that not even the birds in the courtyard wake him.
b5.f3.texto: His slow breathing fills the room like a warm tide.
b5.f4.texto: When he finally opens his eyes, the sun is already high in the window.
b5.f5.texto: He jumps out of bed, puts his shirt on inside out and looks for his shoes.
b5.f6.texto: He goes down the stairs so fast that he almost trips over the cat.
b5.f7.texto: In the street, the fresh air smells of bread and old rain.
b5.f8.texto: Pablo sees the bus from far away and runs to the next corner.
b5.f9.texto: He reaches the office so late that his boss looks at him in silence, with his arms crossed.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Porque» introduces the cause, and here the cause is already given.
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Como» introduces a cause and goes at the start of the sentence.
b6.pregunta: The second part is the result. Which connector is missing?
b7.o0.refuerzo: «O sea que» is for conversation, not for a report.
b7.o1.refuerzo: «Total, que» is colloquial: it is for telling stories.
b7.o2.refuerzo: That is it! It is formal and written in reports and letters.
b7.pregunta: Which connector fits a formal report best?
b8.frase: Tenía tanto sueño que no oí nada
b8.traduccion: I was so sleepy that I heard nothing
b9.o0.refuerzo: «Tanto» goes with nouns or after a verb, not with «cansado».
b9.o1.refuerzo: Well done! Before an adjective you say «tan».
b9.o2.refuerzo: «Muy» does not combine with «que»: «muy cansado que» does not exist.
b9.pregunta: It goes before an adjective. What is missing?
b10.o0.refuerzo: Yes! With a noun, «tanto» agrees in gender and number.
b10.o1: Porque va delante de un adjetivo.
b10.o1.refuerzo: Before an adjective you use «tan», which does not change.
b10.o2.refuerzo: «Gente» is singular; that is why it is «tanta» and not «tantas».
b11.pregunta: Write in Spanish: «There was so much traffic that I was late».
b12.frase: No sonó el despertador. ____ llegué tarde.
b12.o0.refuerzo: «Porque» would give the cause; here the result is needed.
b12.o1.refuerzo: «Como» opens a cause at the start of the sentence.
b12.o2.refuerzo: That is it! «Por eso» gives the result of what came before.
b12.pregunta: It tells the result in speech. What is missing?
p.sales.consejo: Present of «salir», for «tú». Here it means you leave work later today.
p.pasará.consejo: Future of «pasar». Here it means the same thing will happen tomorrow.
p.dormí.consejo: Past tense of «dormir», for «yo». The accent on «í» marks stress.
p.pudimos.consejo: Past tense of «poder», for «nosotros». The «d» is soft between vowels.
p.persiana.consejo: A window blind made of slats. Stress on «SYA».
p.rayas.consejo: Plural of «raya», a line. Starts with a strong «rr».
p.pálidas.consejo: Feminine plural, agreeing with «rayas». Stress on «PA».
p.absoluto.consejo: Stress falls on «LU». It describes «silencio absoluto», total silence.
p.mesilla.consejo: Small table next to the bed. The «ll» sounds like «y».
p.marea.consejo: The rise and fall of the sea. Here it describes slow breathing.
p.salto.consejo: «De un salto» means in one quick jump.
p.revés.consejo: «Al revés» means backwards or inside out. The stress is on the last syllable.
p.deprisa.consejo: A short word for quickly. Stress on «PRI».
p.tropieza.consejo: From «tropezar», to trip. The «z» sounds like «th» in Spain.
p.cruzados.consejo: Participle of «cruzar». «Con los brazos cruzados» means with folded arms.
p.concuerda.consejo: From «concordar», to agree. In grammar, adjectives agree with their noun.
